audit.whatIsWrong: content 'late' says Sett 'has no percent-HP or true scaling on his bar to reclaim it' and whys[6] says 'Sett has no true damage or percent-HP to reclaim the duel'. Both are false, and both are the load-bearing reason the entry gives for why Nasus wins late.
audit.why: Haymaker (W): 'Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides' — the kit's derived flag is literally trueDamage, 'ignores armour and MR — resistances do not help'. Knuckle Down (Q): 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage based off of the target's max health' — that is percent max health, scaling off NASUS's health bar. So Sett has both of the exact two things this entry says he lacks, and both of them specifically punish the way Nasus builds. The recommended item path in report[8] is Trinity Force into Frozen Heart, i.e. armour, against a champion whose burst ignores armour and whose Q gets stronger the more HP Nasus stacks. This is the most dangerous single error in the entry: it tells a player his win condition is out-durabling someone who is built to beat durability. Note the same file already says 'W true-damage smash' in spikes[0] and whys[1], so it contradicts itself.
audit.corrected: Haymaker's centre is true damage and ignores armour; Knuckle Down scales off your max health. Beat him with empowered Q, Spirit Fire shred and lifesteal, not with raw resistances.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (Q Knuckle Down, W Haymaker + trueDamage flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: The Show Stopper is called a suppression in five places: spikes[1] 'R suppress-slam', wants.you[2] 'his R suppress', wants.foe[2] 'all-in with R suppress', mid 'his R suppress-slam', whys[4] 'his R suppress all-in'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Sett carries an enemy champion through the air and slams them into the ground, dealing damage and slowing all enemies near where they land.' That is a carry-and-slam displacement. Suppression is a distinct CC category in League with its own rules, and labelling a displacement as one leads players to make wrong assumptions about how they can respond to it.
audit.corrected: The Show Stopper is a carry-and-slam displacement, not a suppression.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sett.json (R The Show Stopper — flags grounding, hardCC, slow, zone; no suppression)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer treats Facebreaker as a reliable stun ('one E grab into a W smash chunks you', 'Land E grab into stored W'), and dontsFull[1] is titled 'Get E-stunned'.
audit.why: Facebreaker: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' In a clean 1v1 with nothing on his far side, it slows rather than stuns — the stun is conditional on catching things on both sides of him. This is exactly the obscure tech a top laner should be abusing: standing so that he cannot get a two-sided catch downgrades his engage to a slow. The full layer's breakdown.cooldowns already states this correctly, so only the content layer is wrong.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker only stuns if it catches enemies on both sides of Sett; caught alone on one side you are slowed instead.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grit is referenced as 'his grit' and 'stored W' but never explained, so the central trading rule of the matchup is never stated.
audit.why: Haymaker 'passively stores damage he takes as Grit. On cast, Sett expends all stored Grit to gain a shield and punch an area.' The damage Sett takes is what powers the punch he returns — so chipping him in a lane where you cannot kill him actively loads his burst. For Nasus, whose early game is defined by soaking and stacking rather than trading, this is the difference between a safe lane and repeatedly arming the thing that kills him.
audit.corrected: Every point of chip damage you put into Sett is stored as Grit and comes back as Haymaker. Do not poke him for free.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite Haymaker being the entry's designated tracked ability.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12 and Facebreaker is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10. An 18-second Haymaker at rank 1 is a genuinely long window — that is when the fight is takeable, and 'Track Haymaker before every commit' is unactionable without the number.
audit.corrected: Haymaker 18s at rank 1 down to 12s; Facebreaker 16s at rank 1. Fight in the gap after Haymaker is spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged in the packet: Nasus wins 54.35% over 747 games but the content chart gives Sett 5 of 7 stages. Worse, the two layers hold different charts, and the content chart is non-monotonic — Level 6 is 'Skill' and then First item goes back to 'Sett'.
audit.why: content win[] is [Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Skill, Sett, Nasus] while full phases[].side is [Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Sett, Skill, Skill] — they disagree on the last three stages. Nasus's power curve only goes one direction; handing a stage back to Sett after Nasus has already reached parity is the invented power shift the brief warns against, and a player will take a bad first-item fight or refuse a good one. full report[2] meanwhile asserts 'the chart flips at 6 and never flips back', which is true of neither chart. full phases[4] is internally broken too: side is 'Sett' while its own why says 'suddenly the stat-check runs your way. First real fight you're allowed to take.'
audit.corrected: Make it monotonic and consistent across layers: Sett owns levels 1-5, level 6 is Skill, and first item onward is Nasus.

edits.before: Sett owns the first three levels — his passive double-punch and the stored true damage on W hit harder than your bare Q autos before Wither, and one E grab into a W smash chunks you. Don't try to trade back; last-hit at range, lean on Soul Eater lifesteal to stay healthy, and just hoard Q stacks. You have no answer to his grit until you have Wither, so respect his all-in and farm.
edits.after: Sett owns the first three levels — Pit Grit's alternating punches and Haymaker's true damage beat your bare Q autos. Learn how Grit works: Haymaker stores the damage Sett takes, so every point of chip you put into him loads the punch he throws back. Facebreaker only stuns if it catches enemies on both sides of him; caught alone you are just slowed. Last-hit at range, lifesteal the poke, hoard stacks.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay his — he still out-trades you and you're shoving or eating poke while stacking. At 6 it finally evens out: hold Wither for his R suppress-slam, because slowing his attack speed guts his double-punch DPS and Fury of the Sands' bonus HP lets you eat the W smash and live. Don't fight on his terms before then; bait the W, let it whiff or get withered, and only commit when his grab is down.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his — he out-trades you while you stack. At 6 it evens out: hold Wither for The Show Stopper, since slowing his attack speed guts Pit Grit's punch DPS. Your window is Haymaker's cooldown, 18s at rank 1 and 12s maxed, so bait it out, let the Grit empty, and commit only once it is gone. Fury of the Sands' bonus HP covers whatever is left of his burst.

edits.before: This is where you take over. Once your Sheen/Iceborn empowered Q lands and your stacks pile up, his W smash and grit trades stop out-damaging you and you out-durable everything he has. Wither shuts off his only sustained threat, his single grab can't stop a fed splitpusher, and Fury of the Sands wins any prolonged duel. He has no percent-HP or true scaling on his bar to reclaim it — by 2+ items you simply run him over.
edits.after: This is where you take over — but not by out-tanking him. Sett is the wrong target for pure resistances: Haymaker's centre deals true damage that ignores armour outright, and Knuckle Down's bonus scales off your max health, so a fatter Nasus feeds it. Win with empowered Q, Spirit Fire's shred and Soul Eater lifesteal instead, Wither the punch DPS, and time the duel for a Haymaker you have already baited out.

edits.after: Even with Wither up, Facebreaker into a loaded Haymaker out-trades your unempowered Q.

edits.after: Stacked Q, Wither and ult win it — but Haymaker is true damage and Knuckle Down scales off your max HP, so armour won't.

notes: PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING. (1) Four of my edits change level-chart cells: content win[5] 'Sett'->'Nasus' and full phases[4].side 'Sett'->'Skill' are 4-char to 5-char changes, which a naive +/-10% length check will REJECT even though they are the fix for the defect you flagged. phases[5] and phases[6] are 5->5 and will pass. If the applier enforces the band on these enum-like fields, side/win values need an exemption or these will silently no-op and the chart contradiction survives. (2) The two layers currently hold DIFFERENT charts for this matchup — content win[] is [Sett,Sett,Sett,Sett,Skill,Sett,Nasus], full phases[].side is [Sett,Sett,Sett,Sett,Sett,Skill,Skill]. My edits converge both on [Sett,Sett,Sett,Sett,Skill,Nasus,Nasus]. Worth checking whether this content-vs-full chart divergence is systemic across all 71 Nasus entries; if so it is a generator bug, not 71 authoring mistakes. (3) full report[2] says 'the chart flips at 6 and never flips back', which was true of neither chart before my edits and is true of both after — I left it alone deliberately. (4) full report[8] recommends Trinity Force into Frozen Heart. Frozen Heart's attack-speed aura is good against Pit Grit, but its armour does nothing against Haymaker's true-damage centre; I did not propose an item change because I cannot verify current build data from the kit files, but the itemisation line deserves a look now that the 'he has no true damage' premise is gone. (5) The packet suspectName for whys[0], 'No Wither', is a FALSE POSITIVE — Wither is Nasus's own W and is spelled correctly.
